10Then the word of the LORD came to Samuel: 11“I regret that I made Saul king, because he has turned back from following me and has failed to carry out my commands.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out to the LORD all night long. 12Samuel got up early in the morning to meet Saul, and Samuel was told, “Saul went to Carmel and set up a monument for himself there. Then he turned and went on down to Gilgal.” 13When Samuel reached Saul, Saul greeted him, “May the LORD bless you! I have carried out the command of the LORD.” 14Samuel replied, “Then what is this bleating of sheep that fills my ears, and the lowing of cattle that I can hear?” 15Saul answered, “They brought them from the Amalekites. The troops kept back the best of the sheep and cattle as sacrifices for the LORD your God, and everything else we devoted to destruction.”

16“Enough!” Samuel said to Saul. “Let me tell you what the LORD told me during the night.” “Go on,” Saul answered.

17Samuel said, “Even if you were small in your own eyes, are you not head over the tribes of Israel? The LORD anointed you as Israel’s king. 18The LORD sent you on a mission and said, ‘Go and devote to destruction those sinners, the Amalekites. Fight against them until you have wiped them out.’ 19Why did you not obey the voice of the LORD? Why did you pounce on the plunder and do what was evil in the sight of the LORD?”

20Saul said to Samuel, “But I did obey the voice of the LORD! I went on the mission the LORD sent me on. I brought back Agag king of Amalek, and I devoted the Amalekites to destruction. 21From the plunder the troops took sheep and cattle, the choicest of what was devoted to destruction, to sacrifice to the LORD your God at Gilgal.”
22Samuel said, “Is the LORD as pleased with burnt offerings and sacrifices
as with obeying the voice of the LORD?
See, to obey is better than sacrifice,
and to pay heed is better than the fat of rams.
23For rebellion is as sinful as divination,
and arrogance is like wickedness and household gods.
You have rejected the word of the LORD,
so he has rejected you as king.”

24Then Saul said to Samuel, “I have sinned. I have broken the command of the LORD and your instructions, because I was afraid of the troops and gave in to what they said. 25Now please forgive my sin, and come back with me so that I may worship the LORD.” 26But Samuel said to Saul, “I will not go back with you. You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel.”

27As Samuel turned to leave, Saul caught hold of the hem of his robe, and it tore. 28Then Samuel told him, “Today the LORD has torn the kingdom of Israel away from you and has given it to one of your neighbors, one better than you. 29Moreover, the Glory of Israel will not lie or change his mind, for he is not a mortal, that he should change his mind.” 30Saul said, “I have sinned. But please honor me now in front of the elders of my people and in front of Israel. Return with me, and let me worship the LORD your God.” 31So Samuel went back with Saul, and Saul worshiped the LORD.

Samuel puts Agag to death

32Then Samuel said, “Bring Agag king of Amalek here to me.” Agag came to him confidently, and Agag said, “Surely the bitterness of death is past.”

33But Samuel said, “Just as your sword has robbed women of their children, so your mother will be robbed of her child among women.” And Samuel cut Agag to pieces before the LORD at Gilgal.

34Then Samuel went to Ramah, and Saul went up to his home at Gibeah of Saul. 35Samuel did not go to see Saul again until the day he died, though Samuel grieved over Saul. And the LORD regretted having made Saul king over Israel.
fields.summary: Saul is told to destroy the Amalekites but spares King Agag and the best of the livestock. Samuel tells him that obeying is better than sacrifice and that God has rejected him as king.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 16
fields.body_html:
Samuel anoints David

1The LORD said to Samuel, “How long will you go on mourning for Saul, now that I have rejected him from reigning over Israel? Fill your horn with oil and set out. I am sending you to Jesse in Bethlehem, because I have chosen one of his sons to be king for me.” 2Samuel said, “How can I go? Saul will hear of it and kill me.” The LORD said, “Take a young cow with you and say, ‘I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD.’ 3Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I will show you what to do. You will anoint for me the one I name to you.” 4Samuel did what the LORD had said and went to Bethlehem. The elders of the town came out trembling to meet him and asked, “Have you come in peace?” 5He said, “In peace. I have come to offer a sacrifice to the LORD. Make yourselves holy and come with me to the sacrifice.” He made Jesse and his sons holy and invited them to the sacrifice. 6When they arrived, Samuel saw Eliab and thought, “Surely here before the LORD stands his anointed!” 7But the LORD said to Samuel, “Pay no attention to his looks or to how tall he is, because I have rejected him. The LORD does not see in the way a person sees. A person looks at what is there for the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart.” 8Then Jesse called Abinadab and had him walk past Samuel. But Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.” 9Next Jesse had Shammah walk past. But Samuel said, “The LORD has not chosen this one either.” 10Jesse had seven of his sons walk past Samuel, but Samuel said to Jesse, “The LORD has not chosen any of these.” 11Then Samuel asked Jesse, “Are these all the boys you have?” Jesse answered, “There is still the youngest. He is out looking after the sheep.” Samuel said to Jesse, “Send for him and bring him here. We will not sit down to eat until he comes.” 12So Jesse sent for him and had him brought in. He had a healthy, glowing look, with fine eyes, and he was handsome. Then the LORD said, “Get up and anoint him. He is the one.” 13So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him there among his brothers, and the Spirit of the LORD rushed on David from that day on. Then Samuel set out and went back to Ramah.

David plays the lyre for Saul

14Now the Spirit of the LORD had left Saul, and an evil spirit from the LORD tormented him. 15Saul’s officials said to him, “You can see that an evil spirit from God is tormenting you. 16Let our lord give the order to your servants here before you, and they will look for a man who knows how to play the lyre. Then, whenever the evil spirit from God comes on you, he will play and you will feel better.”

17So Saul said to his officials, “Find me a man who plays well and bring him to me.” 18One of the young men replied, “I have seen a son of Jesse in Bethlehem who is a skilled player. He is also a strong warrior and a fighting man. He speaks well, he is handsome, and the LORD is with him.” 19So Saul sent messengers to Jesse with the message, “Send me David your son, the one who is with the sheep.” 20So Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, along with a skin of wine and a young goat, and sent them with his son David to Saul. 21David came to Saul and entered his service. Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer. 22Then Saul sent word to Jesse, “Please let David stay in my service, for I am very pleased with him.” 23So whenever the spirit from God came on Saul, David would take the lyre and play it. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the evil spirit would leave him.
fields.summary: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem, where he anoints David, the youngest son of Jesse, for God looks at the heart. An evil spirit troubles Saul, and David is brought to play the lyre for him.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 17
fields.body_html:
The Philistine champion’s challenge

1The Philistines brought their forces together for war. They assembled at Socoh in Judah and made camp at Ephes-dammim, between Socoh and Azekah. 2Saul and the men of Israel also came together. They pitched camp in the Valley of Elah and formed their battle line facing the Philistines. 3The Philistines held the hill on one side and Israel held the hill on the other, with the valley between them. 4Then a champion came out from the Philistine camp. His name was Goliath, and he was from Gath. He was about 9 feet 9 inches tall. 5He had a bronze helmet on his head and wore a coat of scale armor made of bronze that weighed about 125 pounds. 6He had bronze guards on his legs, and a bronze javelin was slung across his back. 7His spear had a shaft like a weaver’s beam, with an iron head that weighed about 15 pounds. A man carrying his shield walked in front of him. 8He stood and shouted to the ranks of Israel, “Why have you come out and lined up for battle? I am the Philistine, and you are Saul’s servants, are you not? Pick a man for yourselves and let him come down to me. 9If he can fight me and kill me, we will be your slaves. But if I defeat him and kill him, you will be our slaves and serve us.” 10And the Philistine said, “I defy the ranks of Israel today! Give me a man, and we will fight each other.” 11When Saul and all Israel heard what the Philistine said, they were shaken and terrified.

12Now David was the son of that Ephrathite of Bethlehem in Judah whose name was Jesse. Jesse had eight sons, and in Saul’s time he was already old, advanced in years. 13Jesse’s three oldest sons had followed Saul to the war. The names of the three who went to war were Eliab the firstborn, Abinadab the second, and Shammah the third. 14David was the youngest, and the three oldest had followed Saul.

15David went back and forth from Saul’s service to tend his father’s sheep at Bethlehem. 16Meanwhile the Philistine came forward every morning and evening and took his stand, for forty days.

David is sent to his brothers

17Jesse said to his son David, “Please take about 20 quarts of roasted grain and these ten loaves for your brothers, and hurry to the camp with them for your brothers. 18Also take these ten cheeses to the commander of their unit. See how your brothers are doing, and bring back some token from them.” 19Saul was in the Valley of Elah with the brothers and all the men of Israel, at war with the Philistines. 20David got up early in the morning, left the sheep with someone to watch them, loaded up the food, and set out as Jesse had told him. He reached the camp just as the army was going out to its battle positions, shouting the war cry. 21Israel and the Philistines were drawn up, battle line facing battle line. 22David left his load with the keeper of the supplies, ran to the battle line, and went to ask his brothers how they were. 23While he was talking with them, the champion, the Philistine from Gath named Goliath, came up out of the Philistine ranks and spoke the same words as before, and David heard them. 24Whenever the men of Israel saw the man, they all ran from him in great fear. 25The men of Israel were saying, “Have you seen this man coming up? He comes up to defy Israel! The king will give great wealth to the man who kills him. He will give him his daughter as well, and he will make his father’s family free in Israel.” 26David asked the men standing near him, “What will be done for whoever kills this Philistine and removes the disgrace from Israel? This uncircumcised Philistine, who is he, that he dares to defy the ranks of the living God?” 27The troops repeated to him what they had said: “This is what will be done for the man who kills him.” 28When Eliab, his oldest brother, heard him talking to the men, he grew angry with David and said, “Why have you come down here? Who did you leave those few sheep with out in the wilderness? I know your arrogance and the wickedness in your heart. You have come down for nothing but to see the fighting!” 29David said, “What have I done now? Can I not even ask a question?” 30He turned away from him to someone else and asked the same thing, and the troops gave him the same answer as before. 31What David said was overheard and reported to Saul, and Saul sent for him. 32David said to Saul, “No one should lose heart because of this man! Your servant will go and fight this Philistine.” 33Saul answered David, “You cannot go out against this Philistine and fight him. You are a mere youth, and he has been trained for war since his own youth.”

34But David said to Saul, “Your servant has been a shepherd for his father’s flock, and any time a lion or a bear would come and carry off a sheep from the flock, 35I went after it, struck it, and rescued the sheep from its mouth. If it turned on me, I grabbed it by its jaw, struck it and killed it. 36Lions and bears alike your servant has killed, and this uncircumcised Philistine will end up like one of them, since he has defied the ranks of the living God.”

David goes out to meet the Philistine

37David went on, “The LORD rescued me from the power of the lion and of the bear, and he will rescue me from the power of this Philistine.” Then Saul said to David, “Go. May the LORD be with you.” 38Saul dressed David in his own battle clothes. He put a bronze helmet on his head and fitted him with a coat of armor. 39David buckled Saul’s sword over the clothes and tried to move about, since he had never worn such gear. Then he said to Saul, “I cannot walk in all this; I have not tried it before.” And David took it all off. 40He took his staff in his hand, picked out five smooth stones from the streambed, and put them in his shepherd’s bag, in its pouch. Then, with his sling in his hand, he went toward the Philistine. 41The Philistine came on, drawing closer and closer to David, with his shield-bearer in front of him. 42When the Philistine looked David over, he scorned him, because he was only a youth, ruddy and handsome. 43“Am I some dog, that you come after me with sticks?” the Philistine said to David, and he called down curses on David by his gods. 44The Philistine said to David, “Come over here to me, and I will feed your body to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the field!”

45David said to the Philistine, “You have come out against me with a sword, a spear and a javelin. I have come out against you in the name of the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel’s ranks, the one you have defied. 46Today the LORD will hand you over to me. I will strike you down and cut off your head, and this very day I will give the dead bodies of the Philistine army to the birds of the sky and the wild animals of the earth. Then the whole world will know that Israel has a God, 47and everyone gathered here will know that the LORD does not save by sword or spear. The battle belongs to the LORD, and he will hand you over to us.” 48As the Philistine moved forward and came closer to meet David, David ran quickly toward the battle line to meet him. 49David reached into his bag, took out a stone, slung it, and hit the Philistine in the forehead. The stone buried itself in his forehead, and he crashed face down to the ground. 50So David overcame the Philistine with a sling and a stone. He struck the Philistine down and killed him, though David had no sword in his hand. 51David ran and stood over the Philistine. He took hold of the Philistine’s sword, drew it from its sheath, and finished him off; and with it he cut off his head. Seeing that their champion was dead, the Philistines ran. 52Then the men of Israel and Judah rose up with a shout and chased the Philistines as far as the valley and the gates of Ekron. Philistine dead lay along the Shaaraim road all the way to Gath and Ekron. 53When the Israelites came back from chasing the Philistines, they plundered their camp. 54David took the Philistine’s head and brought it to Jerusalem, and he put the Philistine’s weapons in his own tent.

Saul asks whose son David is

55When Saul had watched David going out to meet the Philistine, he had asked Abner, the commander of the army, “Whose son is this young man, Abner?” Abner replied, “As surely as you live, O king, I do not know.” 56The king said, “Find out whose son this young man is.”

57As soon as David came back from killing the Philistine, Abner took him and brought him to Saul, with the Philistine’s head still in his hand. 58Saul asked him, “Whose son are you, young man?” “The son of your servant Jesse of Bethlehem,” David answered.
fields.summary: The Philistine champion Goliath defies Israel’s army. David, sent to his brothers, goes out against him with a sling in the name of God and kills him.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 18
fields.body_html:
Jonathan makes a covenant with David

1When David had finished speaking with Saul, Jonathan’s life became bound up with David’s life, and Jonathan loved him as he loved himself. 2From that day on Saul kept David with him and would not let him go back to his father’s house. 3Jonathan made a covenant with David, because he loved him as he loved himself. 4Jonathan stripped off the robe he had on and handed it to David, together with his battle clothing, and even his sword, his bow and his belt. 5David went out wherever Saul sent him, and he succeeded every time, so Saul put him in charge of the fighting men. This pleased all the people, and Saul’s officials too.

Saul becomes jealous of David

6As the army was coming home, when David returned from killing the Philistine, the women came out from every town in Israel to meet King Saul, singing and dancing with tambourines, with joyful songs and with musical instruments.
7As they celebrated, the women sang to one another,
“Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his tens of thousands.”
8Saul was furious, and this saying displeased him. “They have credited David with tens of thousands,” he said, “and me with mere thousands. What more is left for him but the kingdom?” 9From that day on, Saul watched David with suspicion.

10The next day a harmful spirit from God rushed upon Saul, and he raved inside the house while David was playing the lyre, as he did every day. Saul had his spear in his hand. 11Saul hurled the spear, thinking, “I will pin David to the wall.” But David escaped from him twice. 12Saul feared David, because the LORD was with David and had turned away from Saul. 13So Saul sent him away from his presence and made him commander of a thousand men. David led the army in its campaigns.

14David succeeded in everything he did, for the LORD was with him. 15When Saul saw how very successful David was, he was in dread of him. 16But all Israel and Judah loved David, because he led them in their campaigns.

Saul’s daughters and David

17Saul said to David, “My older daughter Merab is here. I will give her to you in marriage. Only be a brave warrior for me and fight the battles of the LORD.” For Saul thought, “I will not raise my hand against him. Let the Philistines do that.”

18David answered Saul, “Who am I, and what is my family, my father’s clan in Israel, that I should become the king’s son-in-law?” 19But when the time came for Merab, Saul’s daughter, to be given to David, she was given instead to Adriel of Meholah as his wife. 20Now Michal, Saul’s daughter, loved David. When Saul was told about it, he was pleased. 21Saul thought, “I will give her to him so that she can be a trap for him, and the Philistines can kill him.” So Saul said to David, “Today you have a second chance to become my son-in-law.” 22Then Saul gave orders to his officials: “Speak to David privately and tell him, ‘The king is pleased with you, and all his officials love you. Now is the time to become the king’s son-in-law.’” 23Saul’s officials spoke these words to David. But David said, “Do you think it is a small thing to become the king’s son-in-law? I am only a poor man of no importance.” 24Saul’s officials told him, “This is what David said.”

25Saul replied, “Say this to David: ‘The king wants no bride-price except a hundred Philistine foreskins, to take revenge on the king’s enemies.’” Saul was planning to have David killed by the Philistines. 26When his officials told David these words, David was pleased with the idea of becoming the king’s son-in-law. Before the time was up, 27David got up and went out with his men and killed two hundred Philistine men. He brought their foreskins, and they were counted out in full to the king, so that David could become the king’s son-in-law. Then Saul gave him his daughter Michal as his wife.

28Saul saw and understood that the LORD was with David, and that his own daughter Michal loved him. 29Saul became even more afraid of David, and Saul was David’s enemy for the rest of his life.

30The commanders of the Philistines kept coming out to fight, and every time they came out, David was more successful than all Saul’s other officers. So his name became highly honored.
fields.summary: Jonathan loves David and makes a covenant with him. The women’s songs praise David above Saul, Saul grows jealous and tries to kill him, and gives him his daughter Michal as wife.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 19
fields.body_html:
Jonathan speaks up for David

1Saul spoke to his son Jonathan and to all his officials about killing David. But Saul’s son Jonathan was deeply fond of David. 2Jonathan told David, “My father Saul is looking for a way to kill you. So please be careful in the morning. Stay in a hidden place and keep out of sight. 3I will go out and take my place at my father’s side in the field where you are, and talk with him about you. Whatever I find out, I will let you know.”

4Jonathan spoke well of David to his father Saul. “May the king not sin against David his servant,” he said. “David has committed no sin against you, and what he has done has served you very well. 5He took his life in his hands and struck down the Philistine, and the LORD won a great victory for all Israel. You saw it and were glad. So why would you sin against innocent blood by putting David to death for no reason?” 6Saul listened to Jonathan and swore, “As surely as the LORD lives, he will not be put to death.” 7Then Jonathan called David and told him everything that had been said. Jonathan brought David to Saul, and David served him as he had before.

8War broke out again. David went out and fought the Philistines. He defeated them with heavy losses, and they ran from him. 9Then an evil spirit from the LORD came on Saul. He was sitting in his house, spear in hand, while David played the lyre. 10Saul tried to pin David to the wall with the spear, but David slipped away from him, and Saul drove the spear into the wall. David fled and got away that night.

Michal helps David escape

11Saul sent messengers to David’s house to keep watch on him and kill him in the morning. But Michal, David’s wife, warned him, “If you do not escape with your life tonight, tomorrow you will be dead.” 12So Michal let David down through the window, and he went off, fled, and escaped. 13Then Michal took the household god and laid it on the bed. She put a mat of goats’ hair at its head and covered it with a garment.

14When Saul sent messengers to seize David, she said, “He is sick.”

15Then Saul sent the messengers back to see David for themselves. He told them, “Bring him up to me in his bed, so that I can kill him.” 16When the messengers came in, there was the household god on the bed, with the mat of goats’ hair at its head. 17Saul said to Michal, “Why did you trick me like this and let my enemy go, so that he got away?” Michal answered, “He told me, ‘Let me go! Why should I have to kill you?’” 18So David fled and escaped. He went to Samuel at Ramah and reported to him everything Saul had done to him. Then he and Samuel went off and stayed at Naioth. 19Saul was told, “David is at Naioth in Ramah.” 20Saul sent messengers to seize David. But when they saw the company of prophets prophesying, with Samuel standing there as their leader, the Spirit of God came on Saul’s messengers, and they also prophesied. 21When Saul was told, he sent other messengers, and they prophesied too. Saul sent messengers a third time, and they also prophesied. 22Then Saul himself went to Ramah. He came to the great cistern at Secu and asked, “Where are Samuel and David?” Someone said, “They are at Naioth in Ramah.” 23So he went there, toward Naioth in Ramah. The Spirit of God came on him too, and he kept walking along, prophesying, until he came to Naioth in Ramah. 24He too stripped off his clothes, and he too prophesied in Samuel’s presence. He lay there naked all that day and all that night. That is why people say, “Is Saul also among the prophets?”
fields.summary: Jonathan persuades Saul to spare David, but Saul tries to pin David to the wall with a spear. Michal helps David escape, and he flees to Samuel at Ramah.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 20
fields.body_html:
David turns to Jonathan

1David escaped from Naioth in Ramah and went to Jonathan. “What have I done?” he asked. “What is my crime? What wrong have I done to your father, that he is trying to take my life?” 2Jonathan answered, “Never! You are not going to die. My father does nothing, great or small, without telling me. Why would he hide this from me? It is not so.” 3But David answered him with an oath: “Your father knows very well that you think well of me, and he has said to himself, ‘Jonathan must not know this, or it will grieve him.’ But as surely as the LORD lives and as surely as you live, there is only a step between me and death.” 4Jonathan said to David, “Whatever you want, I will do for you.”

5David said to Jonathan, “Listen, tomorrow is the new moon festival, and I am expected to sit at the table with the king. But let me go, and I will hide in the field until the evening of the third day. 6If your father notices that I am missing, tell him, ‘David begged me to let him hurry to Bethlehem, his hometown, because the whole clan is holding its yearly sacrifice there.’ 7Should he say, ‘Good,’ your servant is safe. But should he flare up in anger, you will know that he has made up his mind to do me harm. 8So show faithful love to your servant, because you brought your servant into a covenant with you before the LORD. But if I am guilty, kill me yourself. Why hand me over to your father?”

9Jonathan said, “Never think it! If I knew for certain that my father had decided to bring harm on you, would I not tell you?”

10David asked Jonathan, “Who will let me know if your father gives you a harsh answer?”

11Jonathan said to David, “Come, let us go out into the field.” So the two of them went out together.

12Then Jonathan said to David, “The LORD, the God of Israel, is my witness! By this time tomorrow, or the day after, I will sound out my father. If he is well disposed toward David, I will certainly send word and let you know. 13But if my father means to do you harm, may the LORD deal with me, Jonathan, ever so severely if I do not let you know and send you away to go in safety. May the LORD be with you as he has been with my father. 14And if I am still alive then, will you not show me the faithful love of the LORD, so that I do not die? 15And never cut off your faithful love from my family, not even when the LORD has cut off David’s enemies, every one of them, from the face of the earth.” 16So Jonathan made a covenant with David’s house, and said, “May the LORD call David’s enemies to account.” 17Jonathan had David swear again by his love for him, because he loved him as he loved himself.

18Then Jonathan said to him, “Tomorrow is the new moon festival. You will be missed, because your seat will be empty. 19On the day after tomorrow, go down quickly to the place where you hid when this trouble began, and wait beside the stone Ezel. 20I will shoot three arrows to one side of it, as though I were shooting at a target. 21Then I will send the boy and tell him, ‘Go and find the arrows.’ If I say to the boy, ‘Look, the arrows are on this side of you; pick them up,’ then come, because as surely as the LORD lives, you are safe and there is no danger. 22But if what I tell the young man is, ‘Look, the arrows are beyond you,’ then go, because the LORD is sending you away. 23As for what you and I have agreed, the LORD is witness between you and me forever.”

Saul’s anger at the new moon festival

24So David hid in the field. When the new moon festival came, the king sat down to eat the meal. 25The king sat in his usual seat by the wall. Jonathan got up, and Abner sat down beside Saul, but David’s place was empty. 26Saul did not say a word that day. He thought, “Something has happened to him. He is not ritually clean. Surely he is unclean.”

27But on the next day, the second day of the new moon festival, David’s place was empty again. Saul asked his son Jonathan, “Why has the son of Jesse not come to the meal, either yesterday or today?” 28Jonathan answered Saul, “David begged me to let him go to Bethlehem. 29He said, ‘Please let me go, because our family is holding a sacrifice in the town, and my brother has told me to be there. So if you are willing, let me get away to see my brothers.’ That is why he has not come to the king’s table.”

30Saul’s anger flared up against Jonathan, and he told him, “You son of a perverse and rebellious woman! Do you think I do not know that you have sided with the son of Jesse? It is a disgrace to you and a disgrace to the mother who bore you. 31As long as the son of Jesse lives on the earth, neither you nor your kingdom will be secure. Now send for him and bring him to me, because he must die.”

32Jonathan answered his father Saul, “Why should he be put to death? What has he done?” 33But Saul threw his spear at him to strike him down. Then Jonathan knew that his father was determined to kill David.

34Jonathan got up from the table in a rage and ate nothing on that second day of the festival. He was grieved for David, since his father had shamed him.

The arrows in the field

35Next morning Jonathan went out to the field for the meeting he had arranged with David, and a young boy was with him. 36He said to his boy, “Run and find the arrows I shoot.” As the boy ran, Jonathan shot an arrow beyond him. 37When the boy came to the spot where Jonathan’s arrow had fallen, Jonathan shouted after him, “Is the arrow not beyond you?” 38Then Jonathan shouted after the boy, “Hurry! Be quick! Do not stop!” Jonathan’s boy picked up the arrows and came back to his master. 39The boy knew nothing of what it meant; only Jonathan and David knew. 40Then Jonathan gave his weapons to the boy and told him, “Go, carry them back to town.” 41As soon as the boy had gone, David got up from his place by the south side and fell with his face to the ground, bowing down three times. Then they kissed each other and wept together, and David wept the more. Jonathan said to David, “Go in peace. We two have sworn in the name of the LORD, saying, ‘The LORD will be witness between me and you, and between my descendants and your descendants, forever.’”

42Then David got up and left, and Jonathan went back into the town.
fields.summary: David and Jonathan agree on a sign with arrows to learn Saul’s intentions. When Saul’s anger is clear, they part in tears, bound by their covenant.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 21
fields.body_html:
David comes to Nob

1David came to Nob, to Ahimelech the priest. Ahimelech was trembling as he came out to meet David, and he said to him, “Why are you alone? Why is no one with you?” 2David said to Ahimelech the priest, “The king has given me an order. He told me, ‘No one is to know anything about the mission I am sending you on and the orders I have given you.’ As for my young men, I have told them to meet me at a certain place. 3Now then, what have you got here? Give me five loaves of bread, or anything that can be found.” 4The priest answered David, “I have no ordinary bread on hand, but there is holy bread, provided that the young men have kept themselves from women.”

5David answered the priest, “Truly, women have been kept from us, as always when I set out. The young men’s gear is holy even on an ordinary journey; how much more will it be holy today!” 6So the priest gave him the holy bread, because there was no bread there except the bread of the Presence, which had been taken from before the LORD so that warm bread could be put in its place on the day it was removed. 7Now one of Saul’s officials was there that day, held back before the LORD. His name was Doeg the Edomite, the chief of Saul’s shepherds. 8David asked Ahimelech, “Do you not have a spear or a sword here on hand? I did not bring my sword or any of my weapons with me, because the king’s business was urgent.”

David takes Goliath’s sword and flees to Gath

9The priest said, “Here is the sword of Goliath the Philistine, the man you killed in the Valley of Elah. It lies wrapped in a cloth behind the ephod. Take it if you want it; there is no other sword here but that one.” David said, “There is none like it. Give it to me.” 10That same day David got up and fled from Saul, and he went to Achish king of Gath.
11But Achish’s officials said to him, “Is this man not David, the king of the land? Is he not the one they sang about to one another as they danced,
‘Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his tens of thousands’?”
12David took these words to heart and was greatly afraid of Achish king of Gath. 13So he changed his behavior in front of them and pretended to be insane while he was in their hands. He scribbled on the doors of the gate and let saliva run down his beard. 14Achish said to his officials, “Look, you can see the man is mad. Why have you brought him to me? 15Do I have so few madmen that you bring this fellow to rave in front of me? Should this man come into my house?”
fields.summary: David flees to Nob, where the priest Ahimelech gives him the holy bread and Goliath’s sword. In Gath he pretends to be mad.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 22
fields.body_html:
David at the cave of Adullam

1David left that place and got away to the cave of Adullam. His brothers and his father’s whole family heard about it, and they went down to join him there. 2Men who were in trouble, men who owed money, and men who were bitter about their lot all came to join him, and he became their commander. There were about four hundred men with him. 3From there David went to Mizpah in Moab and said to the king of Moab, “Please allow my father and mother to come out and stay with you until I know what God will do for me.” 4So he took them to the king of Moab, and they lived with him for as long as David was in the stronghold.

5Then Gad the prophet told David, “Do not remain in the stronghold. Leave, and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and came to the forest of Hereth.

Saul kills the priests of Nob

6Saul heard that David and the men with him had been found. Saul was sitting in Gibeah under the tamarisk tree on the height, with his spear in his hand, and all his officials were standing around him. 7Saul said to the officials standing around him, “Listen, you men of Benjamin! Will the son of Jesse give fields and vineyards to every one of you too? Will he make all of you commanders over thousands and over hundreds? 8All of you have plotted against me! No one told me when my son made a covenant with the son of Jesse. None of you feels sorry for me or lets me know that my son has stirred up my servant to lie in wait against me, as he is doing today.”

9Then Doeg the Edomite, who was standing with Saul’s officials, spoke up: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub. 10He asked the LORD for guidance for him, and he gave him food and the sword of Goliath the Philistine.” 11The king sent for Ahimelech the priest, son of Ahitub, and for all his father’s family, the priests at Nob, and they all came to the king.

12Saul said, “Listen now, son of Ahitub.” He answered, “Yes, my lord.” 13Saul said to him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse plotted against me? You gave him bread and a sword and asked God for guidance for him, so that he could rise up against me and lie in wait, as he is doing today.”

14Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your officials is as faithful as David? He is the king’s son-in-law, he has a place in your personal guard, and he is honored in your household. 15Was today the first time I asked God for guidance for him? Far be it from me! Let the king not charge his servant or any of my father’s family with anything, for your servant knew nothing at all about this, small or great.” 16But the king said, “You will certainly die, Ahimelech, you and your father’s whole family.” 17Then the king said to the guards who stood around him, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too have sided with David. They knew he was running away, and they did not tell me.” But the king’s officials refused to lift a hand to strike down the priests of the LORD.

18Then the king said to Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests.” So Doeg the Edomite turned and attacked the priests himself. On that day he put to death eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod. 19He also put Nob, the town of the priests, to the sword. Men and women, children and babies, oxen, donkeys and sheep, he killed them all with the sword. 20But one son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub, whose name was Abiathar, escaped and fled to join David. 21Abiathar reported to David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD. 22David said to Abiathar, “That day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, I knew he would be sure to tell Saul. I am to blame for the death of every person in your father’s family. 23Stay with me and do not be afraid. The one who is after my life is after yours as well. With me you will be kept safe.”
fields.summary: David gathers men at the cave of Adullam. Saul has Doeg kill the priests of Nob, and only Abiathar escapes to David.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 23
fields.body_html:
David saves Keilah

1David was told, “The Philistines are attacking Keilah and looting the threshing floors.” 2So David inquired of the LORD, “Am I to go and attack these Philistines?” The LORD answered David, “Go, attack the Philistines, and rescue Keilah.” 3But David’s men said to him, “Even here in Judah we live in fear. How much worse if we go to Keilah to face the Philistine army!”

4David inquired of the LORD once more, and the LORD answered him, “Set out and go down to Keilah, for I am handing the Philistines over to you.” 5So David and his men went to Keilah and fought the Philistines. He carried off their livestock and dealt them a heavy defeat. So David rescued the people of Keilah.

6Now when Abiathar son of Ahimelech fled to David at Keilah, he came down with an ephod in his hand. 7Saul was told that David had gone to Keilah, and he said, “God has handed him over to me. He has shut himself in by going into a town with gates and bars.” 8Saul called up all the troops for battle, to go down to Keilah and besiege David and his men. 9When David learned that Saul was plotting harm against him, he said to Abiathar the priest, “Bring the ephod here.”

10Then David said, “LORD, God of Israel, your servant has heard for certain that Saul intends to come to Keilah and destroy the town because of me. 11Will the leaders of Keilah hand me over to him? Will Saul come down, as your servant has heard? LORD, God of Israel, please tell your servant.” The LORD answered, “He will come down.” 12David asked again, “Will the leaders of Keilah hand me and my men over to Saul?” The LORD answered, “They will hand you over.”

13So David and his men, about six hundred of them, set out and left Keilah, and they kept moving from place to place. Saul was told that David had slipped away from Keilah, and he called off the march. 14David stayed in the strongholds of the wilderness, in the hill country of the wilderness of Ziph. Saul searched for him day after day, but God did not give David into his hands. 15David saw that Saul had come out to take his life. At the time David was at Horesh in the wilderness of Ziph.

Jonathan strengthens David

16Then Saul’s son Jonathan set out and went to David at Horesh, and he gave him fresh strength in God. 17He said to him, “Do not be afraid. My father Saul will not lay his hand on you. You will reign over Israel, and I will be at your side as your second. Even my father Saul knows that this is so.” 18The two of them made a covenant in the presence of the LORD. Then David stayed on at Horesh, while Jonathan went home.

The Ziphites betray David

19Some Ziphites went up to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Is David not hiding among us? He is in the strongholds at Horesh, on the hill of Hachilah, to the south of Jeshimon. 20So now, O king, come down whenever you wish. Our part will be to hand him over to the king.” 21Saul said, “May the LORD bless you, for you have shown me compassion. 22Go now and make even more certain. Find out exactly where he goes and who has seen him there. I hear that he is very cunning. 23Look into every hiding place he uses and learn them all, then come back to me with sure information. Then I will go with you, and if he is anywhere in the region, I will hunt him down among all the clans of Judah.” 24So they set out and went back to Ziph ahead of Saul. Meanwhile David and his men had gone on to the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah south of Jeshimon. 25Saul and his men went out to look for him. But David was told, so he went down to the rock and remained in the wilderness of Maon. Hearing of this, Saul went after David into the wilderness of Maon. 26Saul moved along one side of the mountain while David and his men moved along the other. David was rushing to get clear of Saul, and Saul and his men were encircling David and his men to capture them. 27But a messenger came to Saul and said, “Come quickly! The Philistines have raided the land.” 28So Saul broke off his pursuit of David and went to face the Philistines. That is why that place was named Sela-hammahlekoth. 29David went up from there and stayed in the strongholds of En-gedi.
fields.summary: David rescues Keilah from the Philistines and escapes Saul in the wilderness. Jonathan strengthens David’s faith, and Saul is called away just as he closes in.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 24
fields.body_html:
David spares Saul in the cave

1When Saul returned from pursuing the Philistines, word was brought to him: “David is in the wilderness of En-gedi.”

2So Saul took 3,000 men chosen from all Israel and set out to search for David and his men east of the Rocks of the Wild Goats. 3He came to the sheep pens along the road. A cave was there, and Saul went in to relieve himself, while David and his men sat far back in the cave. 4David’s men said to him, “This is the day the LORD spoke of when he told you, ‘I am going to give your enemy into your hand, and you may do to him whatever you think best.’” Then David got up and quietly cut off the corner of Saul’s robe. 5Afterward David’s conscience troubled him because he had cut off the corner of Saul’s robe.

6He told his men, “The LORD forbid that I do this to my lord, the LORD’s anointed, and raise my hand against him! He is the LORD’s anointed.” 7With these words David held his men back and would not let them attack Saul. Saul got up, left the cave and went on his way.

8Afterward David also got up, went out of the cave and called after Saul, “My lord the king!” Saul looked back, and David bowed low with his face to the ground and lay prostrate before him.

9David said to Saul, “Why do you listen when people say, ‘David is out to harm you’? 10Today you have seen with your own eyes how the LORD put you into my hands in the cave. I was urged to kill you, but I spared you. I said, ‘I will not raise my hand against my lord, because he is the LORD’s anointed.’ 11My father, look! See the corner of your robe here in my hand! I cut off the corner of your robe, but I did not kill you. You can know for certain from this that I mean you no harm and am not rebelling against you. I have not wronged you, yet you are hunting me down to take my life. 12May the LORD judge between us, and may the LORD avenge the wrong you have done me. But I will not lift my hand against you. 13As the old proverb says, ‘Wickedness comes from the wicked.’ But my hand will not be against you. 14Whom has the king of Israel come out to chase? Whom are you pursuing? A dead dog! A single flea! 15May the LORD be the judge and decide between you and me. May he see this, take up my case and rescue me from your power by giving me justice.”

Saul admits that David is in the right

16When David had finished saying this to Saul, Saul said, “Is that your voice, David my son?” And Saul wept aloud. 17He said to David, “You are more righteous than I am. You have repaid me with good, while I have repaid you with evil. 18Today you have shown how well you have treated me: the LORD handed me over to you, and you did not kill me. 19Who ever finds an enemy and lets him go away unharmed? May the LORD reward you well for the way you have treated me today. 20Now I know that you will surely become king, and that the kingdom of Israel will be firmly established in your hands. 21Now then, give me your oath by the LORD that you will not wipe out my descendants after me or destroy my name from my father’s family.” 22So David gave Saul his oath. Then Saul went back home, while David and his men climbed up to the stronghold.
fields.summary: In a cave at En-gedi David cuts off a corner of Saul’s robe but will not harm the one God anointed. Saul weeps and admits that David is more righteous.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 25
fields.body_html:
The death of Samuel

1Samuel died, and all Israel gathered and mourned for him. They buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David got up and went down to the wilderness of Paran.

Nabal refuses David, and Abigail intervenes

2There was a man in Maon whose property was at Carmel. He was very rich: he owned 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats. And he was shearing his sheep at Carmel. 3The man’s name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was a woman of good sense and beautiful in appearance, but her husband was harsh and his dealings were evil. He was a descendant of Caleb. 4In the wilderness David heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep. 5So David sent ten young men, and he said to them, “Go up to Carmel, go to Nabal and greet him in my name. 6Say this to him: ‘Long life to you! Peace to you, peace to your household, and peace to all that you have. 7I have heard that you are shearing. Your shepherds have been with us, and we did not mistreat them. Nothing of theirs went missing the whole time they were at Carmel. 8Ask your own young men and they will tell you. So let these young men find favor with you, for we have come on a feast day. Please give whatever you have on hand to your servants and to your son David.’” 9When David’s young men arrived, they gave Nabal this whole message in David’s name. Then they waited. 10But Nabal answered David’s servants, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? There are many slaves these days who run away from their masters. 11Am I to take my bread and my water, and the meat I slaughtered for my shearers, and hand it over to men from who knows where?” 12So David’s young men turned around and went back. When they arrived, they reported all these words to him. 13David said to his men, “Every man strap on his sword!” So each of them strapped on his sword, and David strapped on his own as well. About 400 men went up with David, while 200 stayed behind with the supplies. 14Meanwhile one of the young men told Abigail, Nabal’s wife, “David sent messengers out of the wilderness to greet our master, but he flew at them with insults. 15Yet the men were very good to us. We were not mistreated, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we were out in the fields with them. 16They were a wall of protection around us night and day, the whole time we were with them looking after the sheep. 17Now think it over and decide what you should do, because disaster has been decided against our master and against his whole household. He is such a worthless man that no one can speak to him.” 18Abigail acted quickly. She took 200 loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five sheep ready to cook, about a bushel of roasted grain, 100 clusters of raisins and 200 cakes of pressed figs, and loaded them on donkeys. 19She said to her servants, “Go on ahead of me; I will follow you.” But she said nothing to her husband Nabal. 20As she rode her donkey down into a hidden part of the hill, there were David and his men, coming down in her direction, and she came upon them. 21David had just been saying, “It was all for nothing that I protected everything this man had in the wilderness, so that nothing of his went missing. He has paid me back evil for good. 22May God deal with David’s enemies ever so severely if by morning I leave alive a single male of all who belong to him!” 23When Abigail saw David, she quickly got down from her donkey, fell on her face before David and bowed to the ground. 24She fell at his feet and said, “Let the blame be on me alone, my lord! Please let your servant speak to you, and listen to what your servant has to say. 25Please, my lord, pay no attention to this worthless man, Nabal. He is just what his name says. His name is Nabal, Fool, and folly goes with him. But I, your servant, did not see the young men my lord sent. 26Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and as surely as you live, it is the LORD who has kept you from shedding blood and from taking revenge with your own hand. So now, may your enemies and all who want to harm my lord be like Nabal. 27Now let the young men who follow my lord be given this gift that your servant has brought to him. 28Please forgive your servant’s offense. The LORD will certainly make my lord a house that lasts, because my lord fights the battles of the LORD, and no wrong will be found in you as long as you live. 29If anyone rises up to pursue you and to take your life, the life of my lord will be bound safe in the bundle of the living in the care of the LORD your God. But the lives of your enemies he will hurl away as from the pocket of a sling. 30When the LORD has done for my lord every good thing he has promised you, and has made you ruler over Israel, 31my lord will not have this on his mind, no troubled conscience for having shed blood without cause or for having taken revenge himself. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, remember your servant.”

Abigail becomes David’s wife

32David answered Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who has sent you out to meet me today. 33Blessed be your good judgment, and blessed be you, for keeping me today from shedding blood and from taking revenge with my own hand. 34But as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who held me back from doing you harm, if you had not hurried out to meet me, not a single male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by daybreak.” 35Then David accepted what she had brought him from her hand, and told her, “Go back home in peace. I have listened to what you said, and I grant your request.” 36When Abigail came back to Nabal, he was holding a feast in his house, a feast fit for a king. Nabal was in high spirits and very drunk, so she told him nothing at all until daybreak. 37In the morning, when Nabal was sober, his wife told him all this. His heart failed him, and he became like a stone. 38About ten days later the LORD struck Nabal, and he died. 39When David heard that Nabal had died, he said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has taken up my case against Nabal for the insult he gave me, and has kept his servant from doing evil. The LORD has brought Nabal’s evil back on his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking her to become his wife. 40David’s servants came to Abigail at Carmel and said to her, “David has sent us to you to take you to be his wife.” 41She got up and bowed down with her face to the ground, and said, “Your servant is ready to be a maid who washes the feet of my lord’s servants.” 42Abigail quickly got up and mounted her donkey, with her five maids attending her. She followed David’s messengers and became his wife. 43David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel, so both of them became his wives.

44Saul, for his part, had given David’s wife Michal, his own daughter, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
fields.summary: Samuel dies. Nabal insults David’s men, and David sets out for revenge, but Nabal’s wife Abigail stops him with gifts and wise words; Nabal dies, and David marries Abigail.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 26
fields.body_html:
David spares Saul a second time

1Then the Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, “Did you know that David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, which faces the Jeshimon?” 2So Saul got up and went down into the wilderness of Ziph, taking three thousand of Israel’s best soldiers, to hunt for David in the wilderness of Ziph. 3Saul made camp beside the road on the hill of Hachilah, facing the Jeshimon. David was living out in the wilderness, and he realized that Saul had followed him there. 4So David sent out scouts and learned that Saul had indeed arrived. 5Then David set out and came to the place where Saul had made camp. He saw where Saul and Abner son of Ner, the commander of his army, were lying. Saul lay inside the ring of the camp, with the troops camped all around him. 6David turned to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and asked, “Who will go down with me into the camp, to Saul?” “I will go with you,” Abishai answered. 7So David and Abishai went to the troops by night. There was Saul, lying asleep inside the ring of the camp, his spear thrust into the ground by his head, while Abner and the troops lay around him.

8Abishai said to David, “God has put your enemy in your power today. Now please let me drive the spear through him into the ground. One blow is all it will take; I will not need another.” 9But David said to Abishai, “Do not kill him. Who could raise his hand against the LORD’s anointed and not be held guilty?”

10David went on, “As surely as the LORD lives, it is the LORD who will strike him down. Either his time will come and he will die, or he will go out to battle and be cut down. 11May the LORD keep me from ever raising my hand against the LORD’s anointed! Now pick up the spear beside his head and the water jug, and let us be on our way.” 12So David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul’s head, and the two of them left. No one saw them, no one knew, and no one woke up. They were all asleep, because the LORD had sent a deep sleep on them. 13Then David crossed over to the other side and stood on top of the hill some way off, with a wide space between them. 14David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, “Abner, are you not going to answer?” Abner replied, “Who are you, to call out to the king?”

15David said to Abner, “You are a man, are you not? Who else in Israel is like you? Then why did you not guard your lord the king? One of the people came in to kill the king, your lord. 16You have not done well at all. As surely as the LORD lives, you all deserve to die, because you did not guard your lord, the LORD’s anointed. Now look around. Where is the king’s spear, and the water jug that was by his head?” 17Saul recognized David’s voice and said, “Is that your voice, my son David?” David replied, “It is, my lord the king.” 18He went on, “Why is my lord chasing after his servant? What have I done? What wrong have I committed? 19Now please, my lord the king, listen to the words of your servant. If it is the LORD who has stirred you up against me, may he accept an offering. But if it is human beings, may they be cursed before the LORD! For they have driven me out today from my share in the LORD’s inheritance, as if to say, ‘Go, serve other gods.’ 20So now, do not let my blood be spilled on the ground far from the presence of the LORD. The king of Israel has come out to hunt for a single flea, the way someone chases a partridge through the hills.” 21Then Saul said, “I have sinned. My son David, come back. Since you held my life precious today, I will not do you harm again. I have been a fool, and I have done a very great wrong.” 22David answered, “Here is the king’s spear. Let one of your young men come across and get it. 23The LORD repays each person for his righteousness and his faithfulness. Today the LORD put you in my power, but I would not raise my hand against the LORD’s anointed. 24Just as your life mattered greatly to me today, so may my life matter greatly to the LORD, and may he rescue me from every trouble.”

25Then Saul said to David, “Blessed are you, my son David! Whatever you set out to do, you will accomplish it, and you will win in the end.” Then David went his way, and Saul returned home.
fields.summary: David again spares Saul’s life, taking his spear and water jug while he sleeps. Saul confesses his wrong and blesses David.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 27
fields.body_html:
David among the Philistines

1But David said to himself, “One of these days Saul will destroy me. The best thing for me is to escape quickly to the land of the Philistines. Then Saul will give up searching for me anywhere in Israel’s territory, and I will be out of his reach.” 2So David set out and went over with the six hundred men who were with him to Achish son of Maoch, king of Gath. 3David and his men settled with Achish in Gath, each man with his household. David had his two wives with him, Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail of Carmel, Nabal’s widow. 4When word reached Saul that David had fled to Gath, he stopped searching for him.

5Then David said to Achish, “If I have found favor with you, please let me be given a place in one of the country towns, so that I can live there. Why should your servant live in the royal city with you?” 6So that day Achish gave him Ziklag. That is why Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah to this day.

David raids from Ziklag

7David lived in Philistine territory for a year and four months. 8David and his men would go up and raid the Geshurites, the Gizrites and the Amalekites. These peoples had lived in the land from ancient times, in the region that stretches toward Shur and on to the land of Egypt. 9Whenever David attacked the region, he left no man or woman alive. He took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels and clothing, and then came back to Achish. 10When Achish asked, “Did you not go raiding today?” David would answer, “Against the Negev of Judah,” or “Against the Negev of the Jerahmeelites,” or “Against the Negev of the Kenites.” 11David left no man or woman alive to bring to Gath, for he thought, “They might report on us and say, ‘This is what David did.’” This was his practice the whole time he lived in Philistine territory. 12Achish trusted David and thought, “He has made himself utterly hated by his own people, the Israelites, so he will be my servant for life.”
fields.summary: David goes over to the Philistines and settles in Ziklag, raiding Israel’s enemies while Achish thinks he raids Judah.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 28
fields.body_html:
1In those days the Philistines brought their forces together for war, to fight against Israel. Achish told David, “Understand this clearly: you and your men are going out to battle with me, in my army.” 2David answered Achish, “Very well, you will see for yourself what your servant will do.” Achish said to David, “Very well, I will make you my bodyguard for life.”

Saul and the medium at Endor

3Now Samuel was dead. All Israel had mourned for him, and they had buried him in Ramah, his own town. And Saul had removed the mediums and the spiritists from the land. 4The Philistines assembled and came and camped at Shunem, and Saul gathered all Israel, and they camped at Gilboa. 5When Saul saw the Philistine army, he was afraid, and his heart shook violently. 6Saul inquired of the LORD, but the LORD did not answer him, whether by dreams or by the Urim or by prophets. 7Saul told his servants, “Look for a woman who is a medium, so that I may go and inquire through her.” His servants answered him, “There is a woman at Endor who is a medium.” 8So Saul disguised himself by putting on other clothes, and he set out with two men. They came to the woman at night, and he said, “Please consult the spirit for me, and bring up for me the one I name to you.” 9But the woman said to him, “Surely you know what Saul has done, how he has cut off the mediums and the spiritists from the land. Why then are you setting a trap for my life, to get me killed?” 10Saul gave her his oath by the LORD: “As surely as the LORD lives, no punishment will come on you for this.” 11Then the woman asked, “Whom should I bring up for you?” He said, “Bring up Samuel for me.” 12When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed, and she said to Saul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Saul!” 13The king told her, “Do not be afraid. What are you seeing?” The woman answered Saul, “I see a divine being coming up out of the ground.” 14He asked her, “What does he look like?” She said, “An old man is coming up, and he is wrapped in a robe.” Then Saul knew that it was Samuel. He bowed low, face to the ground, and lay down before him.

Samuel’s word to Saul

15Samuel asked Saul, “Why have you disturbed me and brought me up?” Saul answered, “I am in deep trouble. The Philistines are making war on me, and God has turned away from me and answers me no longer, whether through the prophets or in dreams. That is why I have called on you, so that you can tell me what I ought to do.”

16Samuel said, “Why do you ask me, then, when the LORD has turned away from you and become your enemy? 17The LORD has done for himself exactly what he said through me. The LORD has torn the kingdom from your hand and given it to your neighbor, to David. 18Because you did not obey the LORD and did not carry out his fierce anger against Amalek, the LORD has done this to you today. 19The LORD will also hand Israel over to the Philistines along with you. Tomorrow you and your sons will be with me. The LORD will hand the army of Israel over to the Philistines as well.” 20At once Saul fell full length on the ground, terrified by Samuel’s words. There was no strength left in him, because he had eaten nothing all that day and all that night. 21The woman came to Saul and saw that he was badly shaken, and she said to him, “Look, your servant has done what you asked. I took my life in my hands and did what you told me. 22So now, please, listen to your servant in turn. Let me set a little food in front of you. Eat it, so that you will have strength when you go on your way.” 23He refused and said, “I will not eat.” But his servants joined the woman in pressing him, and he listened to them. He got up from the ground and sat on the couch. 24The woman had a fattened calf in the house, and she quickly slaughtered it. She took flour, kneaded it, and baked bread without yeast. 25She set it before Saul and his servants, and they ate. Then they got up and left that same night.
fields.summary: With the Philistines gathering for war and God silent, Saul consults a medium at Endor. Samuel appears and tells him that he and his sons will die the next day.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 29
fields.body_html:
The Philistine commanders send David back

1The Philistines gathered all their forces at Aphek, while Israel was camped by the spring in Jezreel. 2As the rulers of the Philistines marched past with their units of hundreds and thousands, David and his men were marching at the rear with Achish. 3The Philistine commanders asked, “What are these Hebrews doing here?” Achish answered the commanders of the Philistines, “Is this not David, the servant of Saul king of Israel? He has been with me for some time now, a year or more, and from the day he came over to me until today I have found no fault in him.”

4But the Philistine commanders were angry with Achish and said to him, “Send the man back! Let him go back to the place where you stationed him. He is not to go down to battle with us, or he may turn against us once the fighting starts. How could this fellow win back his master’s favor? Surely with the heads of the men here!
5Is this not the David they sang about to one another as they danced,
‘Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his tens of thousands’?”

6So Achish called David and said to him, “As surely as the LORD lives, you have been honest, and I would be glad to have you march out and come back with me in the army. I have found nothing wrong in you from the day you came to me until today. But the rulers do not approve of you. 7So now, go back, and go in peace. Do nothing to displease the rulers of the Philistines.”

8David said to Achish, “But what have I done? What fault have you found in your servant from the day I entered your service until now, that I may not go out and fight the enemies of my lord the king?” 9Achish answered David, “I know that you are as good in my sight as an angel of God. But the Philistine commanders have said, ‘He must not go up with us into battle.’ 10So get up early in the morning, you and your master’s servants who came with you. Start early in the morning, and as soon as it is light, go.” 11So David and his men got up early to set out in the morning and go back to the land of the Philistines, while the Philistines went up to Jezreel.
fields.summary: The Philistine commanders distrust David, and Achish sends him back from the battle.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 30
fields.body_html:
The Amalekites raid Ziklag

1On the third day David and his men reached Ziklag. The Amalekites had raided the Negev and Ziklag. They had attacked Ziklag and burned it down. 2They had taken captive the women who were there, young and old alike. They had killed no one, but had carried them all off and gone on their way. 3When David and his men came to the town, they found it burned down, and their wives, sons and daughters taken captive. 4David and the troops with him wept aloud until they had no strength left to weep. 5David’s two wives had been taken captive too: Ahinoam of Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal of Carmel. 6David was in deep distress, because the troops were talking about stoning him. Each of them was bitter over his sons and daughters. Yet David drew strength from the LORD his God.

David pursues the raiders

7David told Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech’s son, “Bring the ephod here to me, please.” So Abiathar brought the ephod to David. 8Then David inquired of the LORD, “Should I go after this raiding party? Will I catch up with them?” The LORD answered him, “Go after them. You will certainly catch up with them, and you will certainly rescue the captives.” 9So David set out with the 600 men who were with him. They came to the Wadi Besor, where those who were left behind stayed. 10David and 400 men kept up the pursuit, while 200 men stayed behind, too exhausted to cross the Wadi Besor. 11They found an Egyptian out in the open country and brought him to David. They gave him food to eat and water to drink. 12They also gave him a piece of pressed fig cake and two clusters of raisins. When he had eaten, his strength came back, for he had had no food or water for three days and three nights.

13David asked him, “Who do you belong to, and where are you from?” He answered, “I am a young Egyptian, the servant of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago because I fell sick. 14We raided the Negev of the Cherethites, the part that belongs to Judah, and the Negev of Caleb, and we burned Ziklag down.” 15David asked him, “Will you lead me down to this raiding party?” He replied, “Give me your oath by God that you will neither kill me nor hand me over to my master, and I will take you down to them.” 16So he led him down, and there they were, spread out over the whole area, eating and drinking and celebrating over all the great plunder they had taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah. 17From twilight until the evening of the following day David struck them down. Not one of them escaped except 400 young men, who got on camels and fled. 18David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, and he rescued his two wives. 19Nothing of theirs was missing, small or great, sons or daughters, plunder or anything else the raiders had taken. David brought it all back. 20David also took all the flocks and herds. His men drove them ahead of the other livestock and said, “This is David’s plunder.” 21Then David came back to the 200 men who had been too exhausted to follow him and had been left at the Wadi Besor. They came out to meet David and the troops with him, and as David came near, he greeted them.

Equal shares for those who stayed behind

22But every wicked and worthless man in the company that had gone with David said, “Since they did not go with us, we will not give them any of the plunder we recovered. Each man may take his wife and children and go.”

23But David said, “My brothers, you must not act this way with what the LORD has given us. He has kept us safe and has handed over to us the raiding party that came against us. 24Who would listen to you in this matter? The share of the man who stays with the supplies is to be the same as the share of the man who goes down into battle. They will share alike.”

25From that day on it was so: David made it a statute and a ruling for Israel, and it remains so to this day.

Gifts to the elders of Judah

26Back in Ziklag, David sent part of the plunder to the elders of Judah, who were his friends, with the words, “Here is a gift for you, taken from the plunder of the LORD’s enemies.” 27He sent it to those in Bethel, in Ramoth of the Negev and in Jattir, 28to those in Aroer, in Siphmoth and in Eshtemoa,

29to those in Racal, in the towns of the Jerahmeelites and in the towns of the Kenites, 30to those in Hormah, in Bor-ashan and in Athach, 31to those in Hebron, and to all the places where David and his men had moved about.
fields.summary: Amalekites raid Ziklag and take the families captive. David strengthens himself in God, pursues them and recovers everything, and shares the plunder with those who stayed behind.

fields.title: 1 Samuel 31
fields.body_html:
Saul and his sons fall on Mount Gilboa

1Now the Philistines were fighting against Israel. The men of Israel fled from the Philistines, and many fell dead on Mount Gilboa. 2The Philistines caught up with Saul and his sons, and they killed Jonathan, Abinadab and Malki-Shua, Saul’s sons. 3The fighting pressed hard against Saul. The archers found him with their bows, and he was badly wounded by them. 4Saul said to his armor-bearer, “Draw your sword and run me through with it, or these uncircumcised men will come and run me through and make sport of me.” But his armor-bearer would not do it, because he was terrified. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it. 5Seeing that Saul was dead, his armor-bearer also fell on his own sword, and he died with him. 6So Saul died, with his three sons and his armor-bearer and all his men, together on that same day. 7When the men of Israel on the other side of the valley and beyond the Jordan saw that Israel’s army had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead, they abandoned their towns and fled. Then the Philistines came and settled in them.

The men of Jabesh-gilead honor Saul

8On the next day the Philistines came to strip the dead, and they found Saul and his three sons lying where they had fallen on Mount Gilboa. 9They cut off Saul’s head and stripped off his armor, and they sent messengers throughout the land of the Philistines to carry the good news to the temples of their idols and to the people. 10They placed his armor in the temple of the Ashtaroth and fastened his body on the wall of Beth-shan. 11The people living in Jabesh-gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul. 12All their brave men set out and traveled all night. They took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons down from the wall of Beth-shan, brought them to Jabesh, and burned them there. 13Then they took their bones and buried them beneath the tamarisk tree in Jabesh, and they fasted for seven days.
fields.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa, Saul’s sons are killed, and Saul falls on his sword. The men of Jabesh-gilead take the bodies and bury them.

fields.title: Conclusion
fields.body_html:
So Saul died, with his three sons and his armor-bearer and all his men, together on that same day.

— 1 Samuel 31:6

1 Samuel ends on a battlefield. The king the people asked for, the one who stood head and shoulders above them, lies dead on Mount Gilboa beside his sons, and the Philistines hang his body on the wall of Beth-shan. The only kindness left for him comes from the men of Jabesh-gilead, who remember that he once saved their town. And the man God has chosen is far away in Ziklag, in exile.

The question the book leaves with you

Saul is one of the saddest figures in the Bible, and his story is not told to make us despise him. He was brave, and modest at first. But he could not wait for God, and he could not obey him all the way, and when he was found out, he was more concerned for his honour before the people than for what he had done. Little by little he became a man who threw spears at the people who loved him, and at the end he went looking for God’s word in the one place God had forbidden.

David, by contrast, is no saint in 1 Samuel. He lies, he schemes, he nearly takes bloody revenge. But again and again, when the moment comes, he waits for God. He will not kill the LORD’s anointed. He lets Abigail turn him back. At Ziklag, when his own men talk of stoning him, “David drew strength from the LORD his God.”

That is the question 1 Samuel leaves with its readers: not whether we are impressive, but what is in our hearts. “A person looks at what is there for the eyes, but the LORD looks at the heart.” Saul looked like a king. David had a heart that turned toward God, even after it had turned away.

Where the story goes next

2 Samuel opens with David hearing the news of Saul’s death and weeping for him and for Jonathan. It tells how he became king, how God promised him a house for ever, and, with the same honesty, how badly David himself would fall.

The New Testament takes up the thread. Preaching in Antioch, Paul retells this very history: God gave Israel judges “until the time of the prophet Samuel”, then Saul, and then raised up David, “a man in tune with my heart, who will carry out all that I want”, and “From this man’s line God has brought Israel a Savior, Jesus.” Hannah had sung of God’s “anointed” before Israel had a king. Mary sang a song like hers. And Jesus himself pointed to David in this book, eating the holy bread when he and his men were hungry, to show that the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.

Where to go from here

1 Samuel has given the church some of its best-loved preaching on prayer, calling and obedience, and much of it is in this library. A few places to begin:

  • On the whole book. Hannah Whitall Smith’s Old Testament Types and Teachings, whose chapter “1 Samuel: The Kingdom of Man’s Traditions” reads the kingdom the people demanded as a picture of rule by human tradition rather than by God; and Book XVII of Augustine’s The City of God, which reads Hannah’s song, the fall of Eli’s house and the choice of David as prophecies of Christ and his church.
  • On Hannah (1 Samuel 1–2). “Pouring Out the Soul”, on 1 Samuel 1:15, in The Prayers Jesus Learned, an Ochorus Original; and E. M. Bounds’s Prayer and Praying Men, with its chapter “Samuel, the Child of Prayer”.
  • On the call of Samuel (1 Samuel 3). Alexander Maclaren’s sermon The Child Prophet (1 Samuel 3:1–14) and John Henry Newman’s Divine Calls (1 Samuel 3:10).
  • On Samuel’s intercession (1 Samuel 12). “The Sin of Not Praying”, on 1 Samuel 12:23, in The Prayers Jesus Learned.
  • On Saul and obedience (1 Samuel 13–15). Andrew Murray’s The School of Obedience, whose chapter “Obedience: Its Place in Holy Scripture” dwells on Saul’s failures and Samuel’s verdict; and A. B. Simpson’s The Holy Spirit, or Power from on High, whose chapter “The Holy Spirit in the Lives of Saul and David” sets the two kings side by side.
  • On David and Goliath (1 Samuel 17). Phillis Wheatley’s poem “Goliath of Gath”, in Poems on Various Subjects.
  • For reading with children. “Hannah’s Prayer”, “David and the Giant”, “David and Jonathan” and “David Spares the King” in Tell Me the Story – Book 3: Kings and Prophets, and “A King Like the Nations” in The Big Story, both Ochorus Originals.

You can also go the other way, from the text to the classics. Every reference to 1 Samuel in this library can be tapped to read the verse, and the Scripture pages gather, chapter by chapter, what the great writers of the church have said about each passage of this book.

And then read on into 2 Samuel, where David’s long wait ends. But first, stand for a moment with Samuel at Mizpah, beside the stone he set up after the LORD had rescued his people once again, and say with him what every believer can say at every stage of the journey:

Then Samuel took a single stone and placed it between Mizpah and Shen. He called it Ebenezer and said, “To this point the LORD has helped us.”

— 1 Samuel 7:12
